Alright kids, settle down for a bit. I want to tell you a story about when I was a little girl, not much older than you two. I used to love playing with my grandmother's old typewriter. Ah'm made a lovely cuppa, so ah have. Would yer like one, Mum? Dad? It's a nice strong brew, just the way yer like it. Ooh, thank ye, lass. That's very kind of yer. I'll 'ave a cup, please. Alright kids, who's excited about Shakespeare week coming up? We're going to learn all about his plays and even get to visit Stratford to see a performance. I am! I am! I'm telling you, it was the most harrowing experience of my life, being arrested in Jeddah for trying to sail a boat to Cyprus. But it was interesting to see how different countries approach the subject of alcohol. I've found that some countries are much more relaxed about it, while others are very strict. That's true. I'm telling you, it's been a nightmare getting the bathroom renovated. The contractor keeps delaying the job, and I'm starting to think we'll never have a decent shower again. I feel your pain, love. Ey up, I'm starvin'! When are we stoppin' for some scran? I've 'eard great things about the food 'ere in Istria. Ah, pet, we'll stop soon, don't worry. I'm so glad we decided to grab lunch here, the Printing House has such a lovely atmosphere. I've always been fascinated by the history of Cambridge University Press. I think language is one of those things that's easy to take for granted, but it's so important for conveying meaning and ideas. I'm so excited to finally arrive at Sarah's house in Tarnow, I've been looking forward to this visit for weeks. How's the GPS saying we're doing for time? Ah'm tellin' ye, pet, that new football strip design is canny. The colours are spot on, like. What do ye think, lass isn't here, but you are, so I'm askin' you? Cheers, love. Blimey, I'm so glad we're havin' a cuppa and a chat, innit? I feel like I haven't seen you in ages, bro. How's life been treatin' ya? Ah, you know, just the same old, same old. I'm so glad we're having a chance to catch up over coffee, it feels like it's been ages. How was your week, Karen? It's been alright, just been keeping busy with work and whatnot. You know how it is. Hey, Emily! I'm so glad you're over. I've had the most chaotic week at school. We just got back from a maths test and I'm pretty sure I messed it up. Ah, don't worry, Sophie! I'm telling you, the Matrix is like a religion. It's all about questioning reality and finding the truth. I mean, have you seen the movie? Oh, Alex, you and your sci-fi films. Ey up, I'm gettin' a bit parched. Can we stop for a drink soon? I've 'eard there's a lovely market in Poreč where we can grab some fresh orange juice. That sounds like a great idea, love. I had the most wonderful conversation with Sarah the other day. You know, she's just had her baby, and I was asking her all about it. I must say, I'm a bit broody now. Ah, yeah! I can imagine. Isn't it lovely to get out of the city and into the countryside? The fresh air is doing me a world of good. Dad, I'm so glad I'm finally home for a bit. I've been meaning to ask you, have you considered getting a new mobile phone? Yours is ancient. Ah, what's wrong with my old one? I'm telling you, it's a absolute travesty what they're planning to do with the local library. I mean, can you believe they're considering demolition? I agree. It's all about compromise, I suppose. But, in the case of the library, I think we should fight to save the whole building, not just the facade. We should write to the local council and express our concerns.

I'm telling you, the best music festival I've ever been to was Glastonbury back in '92. The atmosphere was electric, and the lineup was incredible. I mean, who can forget Nirvana's performance? Ah'm tellin' thee, lad, gettin' car insurance as a young driver is a right ol' headache. Tha'll be payin' through tha nose, so tha will. An' it's not just t'premiums tha's got to worry about, it's t'cost o' t'car itself, petrol, maintenance... it all adds up, y'know. When I were learnin' to drive, it were a lot simpler. Less traffic on t'roads, an' insurance were a fraction o' t'cost. Yeah, I've been thinkin' about gettin' an old banger, just sommat to get me around. But then I've 'eard some o' them older cars can be more expensive to insure because they don't 'ave all t'modern safety features an' that. That's right, lad. On t'other hand, if tha gets a better car, it'll be more expensive, but it might be worth it in t'long run. I reckon tha should do some research, look at different options, an' see what suits thee best. Alright, I'll do that. An' what about them black box things, Mum? Do you think they're any good? Ah, you mean t'telematics boxes? They can be a good way to reduce t'cost o' insurance, especially for young drivers. They track tha driving habits an' if tha drives safely, tha can get a discount on tha premium. Lads, I'm tellin' ye, work's been a nightmare lately. The stress is killin' me. I don't know how much more of it I can take. What's wrong, uncle? You always seem so calm and collected. And apparently, your heart rate and blood pressure can indicate your stress levels too. That's cool! I've done those quizzes before. They're pretty accurate, I think. By the way, have you heard about the Irish present? Ah, you mean the children's allowance? I think you have to be a resident for a certain amount of time to be eligible. That's right. I was talkin' to a friend the other day, and she was sayin' how different it is here compared to England. Yeah, I've noticed that too. Like, with the equality vote and all that. It's really interesting to see how different countries approach the same issues. Absolutely. And it's great to see Ireland takin' steps in the right direction. Although, it's funny... sometimes I'll be talkin' to someone, and there'll be this awkward silence... Oh, don't I know it! It's like, you're thinkin', "What do I say next?" Yeah, it's so awkward! By the way, are we bein' recorded or somethin'? No, no, nothin' like that! Although, I did listen to this podcast the other day, and it was really interesting. Ooh, what was it about? It was about the importance of communication in partnerships. Speakin' of which, how's school goin', lad? It's goin' alright, I s'pose. Just gettin' back into it after the holidays. Hey, can we get a Chinese takeaway tonight? You and your love of Chinese food! Alright, alright, we can get one. But I'm tellin' ye, the quality of the chicken in that curry last time was dreadful. Ah, come on! It wasn't that bad! You're just bein' picky. I am not! I'm just sayin', if you're goin' to use words like "dreadful", you should be prepared to back 'em up with some emotion and facial expressions.

Ey up, Mum, have you seen that new bird sanctuary they've built near the hilltop village we visited last summer? I was thinkin' we could stop by on the way back from our trip. Ah, yes, love! I've 'eard it's lovely this time of year. The weather's been perfect for a day out, hasn't it? Although, I'm a bit worried about the forecast for the rest of the week. They're sayin' there might be some heavy rain. Can we go to the sanctuary, please? I wanna see the birds! And can we drive up to the hilltop village afterwards? I love lookin' out at the view from the top. Of course, lad, we can definitely fit that in. By the way, I was talkin' to a colleague the other day about law conversion courses. Have you thought about pursuin' a career in law, Emily? Actually, yeah, I 'ave been thinkin' about it. actually, I've been lookin' into it, but I'm not sure if it's the right path for me. I was thinkin' we could weigh our options and see what's available. Do you know 'ow much that picnic basket weighs, John? Hmm, let me check... I think it's about 5 kilograms. Or is that 5,000 grams? I always get those two mixed up. That's easy, Dad! Just remember, 1 kilogram is 1,000 grams. And we should probably convert the distance to the sanctuary into kilometers instead of miles. It's about 10 kilometers, right? Yeah, that's right! And speakin' of distances, I was thinkin' about the EU referendum and 'ow it'll affect travel. Do you think it'll make it 'arder to visit other countries? Well, I'm not sure, love. But I do know that it's caused a lot of controversy. Just like 'ow some people believe in Bear Grylls' survival methods, while others think 'e's just a bit crazy. I think 'e's cool! I love watchin' 'is shows.

I'm telling you, I've been considering going vegetarian for months now. I just can't stomach the thought of all those poor animals being slaughtered for our benefit. I totally get it, Em. I've been a veggie for years, and it's been one of the best decisions I've ever made. Not just for the animals, but for the environment too. Have you seen those documentaries on the meat industry? Ah, yeah, don't get her started on that. She's been forcing us to watch all sorts of stuff on Netflix. But seriously, it's pretty eye-opening. I've been thinking about reducing my meat intake too. Exactly! And it's not just about the animals. It's about the resources it takes to produce meat, the deforestation, the water waste... it's just so unsustainable. Actually, from what I've read, it's supposed to be pretty similar to real meat, just without the, you know, animal bits. And it's not like we don't already eat plenty of processed foods. I mean, have you seen the ingredients list on some of those vitamin tablets we take? Oh, don't even get me started on those. I'm pretty sure I've been taking the same multivitamins since I was a teenager, and I have no idea what half the stuff in them does. But anyway, back to the meat thing... I think it's really interesting that you're considering going veggie, Em. What made you start thinking about it? Well, it's just been on my mind a lot lately, I suppose. Ey up, lads and lasses, what's on t'telly tonight then? Any decent films or is it just rubbish? Ah, I think there's a Marvel film on later, but I'm not sure which one. I've been meanin' to get a passport an' start travelin' more, but y'know, it's hard when y'have no job an' no money. That's true, but maybe we could all save up an' go on a trip together? That would be a right laugh. An' speakin' of laughs, have y'seen that new comedy film that's out?

Oh, it's so lovely to see you here at the Alumni Day, Emily! I feel like we haven't caught up in ages. How's life been treating you? It's great to see you too, Sarah! Ah'm tellin' thee, I'm fair knackered after that lecture today. Three hours of psychology an' ah'm still tryin' to process it aall. How were yer classes, then? Ah, y'know, same old same old. Now, let's get this essay sorted, an' then we can start thinkin' about more fun things... like that massage, an' maybe a weekend away to the Dales? Ooh, that sounds perfect! I'm telling you, the state of the news these days is just appalling. Have you seen the latest on the migrant crisis in Calais? It's heartbreaking, the conditions those people are living in. Ah, good morning, I see you're enjoying a cup of coffee. I'm afraid I'm in desperate need of one myself after the morning I've had. Just got back from a decorators' disaster at my place. Alright kids, gather around. Today we're going to talk about different metals and fabrics. You know how we've been playing Minecraft and collecting all those valuable resources? I'm so glad we decided to meet up here at the Seven Stars Pub, it's been ages since we caught up properly. How was your Christmas, then? Did you manage to get away anywhere nice? I might have to check it out and see if it's something I can recommend to my students. Speaking of which, how's your sister doing? I remember you saying she was expecting a baby. Ah, yes! She's doing great, thanks for asking.

Ah, lovely day for a stroll around the garden, isn't it? I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen any birds nesting in the trees lately? Oh, yes! I saw a robin building a nest in the oak tree just last week. I've been putting out some seeds and worms for them, and they seem to be enjoying it. You know, I've also been thinking of putting up some new feeders. What do you think, dear? That's a wonderful idea! I've been noticing the birds have been visiting our garden more frequently since we started putting out the bird feeders. And I must say, it's been a delight to watch them. By the way, would you like another slice of cake? I made it myself, and I think it's still fresh. Ah, thank you, dear. I'd love another slice. You know, I was just thinking about my childhood, and I remembered this wonderful puppet show I used to watch. It was all about birds and their habitats. I wonder if they still make shows like that for children. Oh, I'm sure they do! Although, I think they're more into these new-fangled computer animations these days. But, you know, there's something charming about traditional puppetry. I've been meaning to ask you, how's your diabetes been? Have you been keeping an eye on your sugar levels? Yes, he has. And I've been making sure he's eating properly, too. Although, it's not always easy, is it? I mean, when you're retired, it's easy to get into bad habits. Speaking of which, have you seen that new community center they're building for old people? I heard it's going to have all sorts of facilities, including a garden and a cafeteria. Ah, yes! I saw it in the paper. It sounds like a wonderful idea. We should definitely go check it out when it's finished. You know, it's nice to have places like that for people our age to socialize and stay active. And maybe they'll even have some bird-watching groups or something! Ha! That would be perfect. Although, I think we're doing all right for ourselves, just walking around the garden and enjoying the fresh air. And, of course, having a nice cup of tea and some cake.

I'm so glad we decided to meet up for lunch, it's lovely to catch up with you. Have you been to this restaurant before? The food smells amazing. Ah, yes, I have. The owner, Andreas, is a friend of a friend. The moussaka here is to die for. What do you fancy trying? That sounds great, I'll have the moussaka then. And a glass of white wine, please. How's your summer been so far? We've been keeping busy with the pets, haven't we? My cat, Luna, has been getting into all sorts of mischief. I'm sure she has. My dog, Max, has been enjoying the sunshine. I've been taking him on long walks along the beach. You know, I saw the most interesting couple come in here yesterday. They were both wearing matching "I love Cyprus" t-shirts. I kid you not. That's hilarious. I love people-watching. My sister, Rachel, would love it here. She's always been fascinated by different cultures. Speaking of which, how's your family? I feel like I haven't seen your wife, Sarah, in ages. How's she coping with her mother's illness? Ah, yes, it's been tough. Her mother's been in and out of hospital, but we're all trying to stay positive. You know, it's funny, I was talking to Sarah the other day, and we were both saying how we're at that age where we're starting to lose people. My uncle passed away last year, and it was a real shock. I'm so sorry to hear that. Losing loved ones is never easy. I've been thinking about my own mortality a lot lately, and I've been exploring some spiritual practices. Have you ever heard of shamanism? Actually, I have. I've been reading about dowsing and how it can be used to connect with the natural world. It's fascinating stuff. I've even tried it out a few times. Do you think it's possible to tap into some kind of collective destiny? That's exactly what I've been thinking about. I feel like we're all connected, and that our lives are intertwined in ways we can't even imagine. It's like we're all part of some bigger web. And have you noticed how we keep meeting new people who seem to be on a similar journey to us?

Mum, it's so great to be back home. I've missed your cooking so much. What's for lunch today? Ah, darling, I'm glad you're home. I was thinking of making some sandwiches and soup. Your father and I were just discussing our plans for Christmas. We were thinking of getting your grandparents over for dinner this year. That's a great idea, love. We should start making arrangements for it sooner rather than later. I was thinking we could also invite some of our close friends over for a Christmas party. What do you think, dear? That sounds like a lot of fun, Dad. I'd love to help with the planning. By the way, how's work been? How's the farm doing? It's been keeping me busy, as usual. We've had some issues with the weather, but overall, it's been a good year. I've been thinking of making some changes to the business, maybe expanding into new markets. That sounds exciting, dear. You'll have to tell us more about it over lunch. Emma, how's your job as a project coordinator going? Are you enjoying it? It's been a challenge, but I'm really enjoying it. I've been learning a lot and working with a great team. We've been talking about our living situation, and I was thinking of moving into a new flat with some friends. Ah, that's great news, Emma. We'll have to come visit you once you're all settled in. What's the new place like? It's really nice, Dad. It's got a big garden and a lovely living room. We're all very excited about it. Speaking of which, I was thinking of having a housewarming party and I'd love it if you both could come. Of course, dear, we wouldn't miss it for the world. We'll have to bring some of our famous Christmas cookies. And I'll bring some of my famous rugby jokes. Did you hear the one about the rugby player who walked into a bar? No, Dad, I don't think I have. Tell us. Okay, here it goes: Why did the rugby player bring a pillow to the party? I don't know, why? In case he needed a soft defense! Dad, that's so cheesy. Oh, stop it, you two.

Ey up, lasses! 'Ave you seen that Jeremy Kyle show where they catch out all them catfish? It's mental, int it? Ah, yeah! I watched it last week, lah. This one bloke was convinced 'e was talkin' to a supermodel, but it turned out to be some lad from down the street with a fake profile. I felt so sorry for 'im, though. I know, right? It's like, how can people be so gullible? But at the same time, it's easy to get caught up in the idea of sommat that seems too good to be true. I've 'ad a few mates who've been catfished before, and it's a right mess to sort out. Exactly! And it's not just the catfishin' that's the problem, it's the emotional manipulation, an' all. These people are preyin' on others' vulnerabilities, and it's just not on. I mean, I've 'eard of people sendin' money to these fake profiles, and it's just heartbreaking. That's the worst part, int it? When they start sendin' money or personal info, it's like, they're puttin' themselves in so much danger. And Jeremy Kyle's always goin' on about how they should've been more careful, but it's easy to say that when you're not the one in the situation. Yeah, and it's not just about bein' careful, it's about bein' kind, too. I mean, we've all been in situations where we've trusted someone and it's turned out badly, but that doesn't mean we should be judgmental about others who've made the same mistake. We should be supportin' each other, not tearin' each other down. Definitely, yeah. So, 'ave you two ever 'ad any experiences with catfishin' or online scams? Any close calls or near misses? Well, I did 'ave a weird experience once where someone was tryin' to get me to send 'em money, but I realized it was a scam pretty quickly. I reported it to the site, and they sorted it out, but it was a bit of a shock, to be honest. I've 'ad a few weird messages from people, but nothin' that's ever seemed like a proper scam. Just the usual weirdos and trolls, you know? But I do know someone who got catfished on a dating site, and it was a right mess.

Blimey, this pasta's lovely, thanks for cookin' it up for us. I was thinkin' about our trip to Paris the other day, and I really wanna go back. The Eiffel Tower was amazin'. Ah, Paris, the city of love! I'm so glad you enjoyed it, dear. You know, I've been thinkin' about learnin' some more languages myself. I've been meanin' to brush up on my Italian, considerin' my birthplace is just near the border. Vienna's not far from Italy, you know. That's really cool! I've been thinkin' about learnin' German, actually. I've got a mate who's studyin' German at uni, and he says it's a right challenge. But I reckon it'd be worth it, especially with your background and all. Ah, German's a wonderful language! I grew up speakin' it, of course, bein' from Vienna and all. My family used to take these lovely trips to the Italian countryside, and I just fell in love with the place. You should totally come with me next time, dear. I'd love to! I've been meanin' to ask, how's your art comin' along? Have you been workin' on any new pieces? And by the way, I was thinkin' about my own studies – I'm thinkin' of takin' a course on Classics next semester. Oh, my art's been keepin' me busy, that's for sure! I've been workin' on this lovely piece inspired by the bees in our garden. They're such fascinatin' creatures, don't you think? And Classics, you say? That sounds like a wonderful subject. I've always been fascinated by ancient history myself. Yeah, I've always been interested in it, and I reckon it'll be a great way to learn more about the roots of European culture. Speakin' of which, have you ever been to Italy just to explore the ancient ruins and whatnot? Oh, many times, dear! Italy's full of history, and I just love gettin' lost in the old cities. You should totally come with me sometime, and we can explore all the ancient wonders together. By the way, have you had a chance to look at my computer? I've been havin' some trouble with it, and I could use a young tech-savvy person like yourself to help me sort it out. Course, I'll take a look!

Blimey, look at that driver, he's all over the road. I'm getting a bit anxious, aren't you, Dad? Ah, don't you worry, love, I've been driving for years. I know what I'm doing. Although, I have to say, some of these new drivers are a menace. No respect for the road or other drivers. I know what you mean. I was driving to work the other day and this young lad cut me off. I was shocked. And to think, he was on his phone at the same time. It's terrifying. Exactly! It's like they think they're invincible or something. Anyway, enough about that. How's your day been so far, Mum? You had a day off work, didn't you? Yes, I did. It was lovely. I got to sleep in and then I went out for a bit of lunch with some friends. We had a nice time chatting and catching up. Although, I did have to make a few phone calls to sort out some things with the solicitor. Oh, what's going on with the solicitor? Everything okay? Yeah, everything's fine. Just some paperwork to sort out. You know how it is. But, on a more exciting note, have you seen that new building that's going up on the outskirts of town? It's huge! No, I haven't. What's it going to be? A new shopping center or something? I think it's going to be some new offices. But, apparently, it's going to be really swanky. All modern and high-tech. I'm not sure I like the sound of that. All these new buildings and developments are changing the face of our town. And have you seen the state of some of the towns around here? Some of them are right dumps. Oh, come on, Dad. You can't say that. Every town has its own character. Although, I do have to say, some of the towns we've driven through on our way to Dorset have been a bit... rough around the edges. Yes, that's true. But, at the end of the day, it's the people that make a town, not the buildings or the streets. Speaking of which, have you had your car's MOT done recently? Ah, yes. I had it done last week. All passed with flying colors.

Blimey, I'm getting on a bit, aren't I? Seventy-five and still kicking, but I feel like I'm losing me touch with the world. What's the point of having all this technology if I don't know how to use it, eh? Oh, come on, love! You're not that old! You're still sharper than most people half your age. And don't worry about the technology, I'm still trying to figure it out myself. I mean, have you seen these new smartphones? They're like mini computers or something! Sharper than most people half me age? Ha! I doubt that. I feel like I'm stuck in the dark ages, mate. I didn't even finish me education, you know. Left school at fifteen and never looked back. Or at least, that's what I thought at the time. Now I'm not so sure. Well, you've done all right for yourself, haven't you? I mean, we've had our ups and downs, but we've always managed to get by. And you've got me to look after you now, don't you? So, what's the worry? The worry is that I've never done anything with me life, that's what. I've just existed, really. Never had a proper job, never achieved anything. I feel like I've wasted me time, if you know what I mean. Oh, don't be daft! You've had a good life, and we've had some great times together. And what's this nonsense about not achieving anything? You've got me, haven't you? And I'm proud of you, no matter what. Thanks, love. That means a lot coming from you. But I still can't help feeling like I've missed out on something. I mean, all me mates from school, they all went on to do great things. Some of them even went to university! Can you imagine? Well, maybe they did, but that doesn't mean they're any happier than you are. And besides, you've got your own unique experiences and stories to tell. That's what matters, not some piece of paper or a fancy job title. I suppose you're right, as always. You've got a way of putting things into perspective, don't you? But I still wish I could've done things differently.

Ah'm tellin' ye, pet, the weather's been canny weird lately. One day it's pourin' down, the next it's sunny skies. Makes it hard to plan oot a gardenin' schedule, y'knaa? I know what you mean, love. I was tryin' to get some work done in the garden yesterday, but the sun was beatin' down on me somethin' fierce. I had to take a break and come in for a cold drink. By the way, how's the research comin' along at work? It's goin' alrigh', thanks for askin'. We're gettin' some interestin' results, but nothin' conclusive yet. I'm more excited about the gig we're goin' to this weekend, though. Have ye heard of the band that's playin'? Ah, yeah! I've heard of 'em. They're a folk-group from Scotland, aren't they? I've got a mate who's into that sort of thing, and he's always ravin' about 'em. That's the ones! I've been listenin' to their album nonstop, and I'm really lookin' forward to seein' 'em live. We should get the gang together and make a night of it. How's yer PhD comin' along, by the way? Still buryin' yer head in books? Yeah, somethin' like that. It's a lot of work, but it's worth it in the end, I think. I'm just tryin' to get this paper finished, and then I can take a bit of a break. Maybe we can plan a BBQ or somethin' for when the weather settles down? Sounds like a grand idea, pet! I've been meanin' to get the garden sorted oot, anyway. We can get some plants in, and maybe even try our hand at growin' some vegetables. I've been readin' about this new method of companion plantin' that's supposed to be really effective. That sounds fascinatin'. I've always been interested in gardenin', but I don't know much about it. You'll have to teach me the ropes, love. Maybe we can even get some of our friends over to help us get started. Aye, that'd be great! We can make a day of it, and then have a big dinner together afterwards. I'll start lookin' into it, and we can plan somethin' for next weekend. Oh, and speakin' of music, have ye heard from Sarah lately?

Ah'm tellin' ye, it's a right mess out there for young people lookin' for work. The unemployment rates are through the roof, pet. Ah've been readin' about it a lot for me research project at the university. I know, it's devastating. I've got mates who've just graduated and they're really strugglin' to find a job in their field. And to think we're complainin' about the tuition fees we paid, it's even worse now. They're payin' nine grand a year! What's the point of gettin' a degree if you can't even get a decent job afterwards? Exactly! And it's not like they're not qualified or anythin'. It's just that there aren't enough jobs to go around. Ah've been lookin' at the statistics, and it's alarming how many graduates are endin' up in low-skilled jobs or on benefits. It's a waste of their potential, if ye ask me. And have you seen the news about the latest cuts to the university budgets? It's like they're tryin' to price people out of education altogether. I mean, I was lucky to get me PhD funded, but I know people who are strugglin' to make ends meet while they're studyin'. It's a real challenge. Aye, it's a nightmare. But, on a more positive note, have ye heard about the new musical that's comin' to the West End? Ah've heard it's amazin', and ah'm dyin' to see it. We should get tickets and make a weekend of it in London. You and your love of musicals! Ah'd love to see it, but we should probably wait till ah've finished me thesis. Can't have too many distractions, ye know? But, speakin' of which, did ah tell ye about the time ah saw Les Misérables in Birmingham? It was incredible! The theater was packed, and the performin' was top-notch. Ye've told me about it a few times, but ah don't mind hearin' it again! Ye should take me to see it sometime, and we can make a night of it. By the way, how's yer thesis comin' along? Are ye makin' good progress? Ah, it's goin' alright, thanks for askin'. Just tryin' to get me head around all the research and get it down on paper. It's a lot of work, but it'll be worth it in the end.

Mum, I've been thinking about writing a kids' book, and I wanted to get your opinion on it. I was looking at some pictures and I thought it would be really cool to create a story around them. That sounds like a great idea, love! I'd be happy to help you brainstorm. What kind of story were you thinking of? Is it going to be about adventure, magic, or something else? I'm not entirely sure yet, but I was thinking maybe something about a family tree. You know, with all the different characters and their relationships. It could be really interesting to explore all the different family dynamics. Oh, I couldn't help but overhear. A family tree story, you say? That's a great idea! I used to teach my students about family trees and how to research their own heritage. It's such a wonderful way to learn about where you come from. Yes, it's so important for kids to understand their roots and the different relationships within their family. I've been trying to get the boys interested in our family history, but they're not really biting... yet! Yeah, I know what you mean. My brothers are always like, "Mum, do we have to?" But I think if we make it fun and engaging, they might actually start to take an interest. Absolutely! And that's where your book comes in, dear. You could make it a fun, interactive way for kids to learn about their family tree. Maybe include some puzzles or games to help them understand the different relationships. That's a fantastic idea! And we could even include some stories about our own family. You know, about your dad and me, and how we met. Or about my parents and their experiences. Yeah, that would be really cool. I could interview you both and get some stories to include in the book. And maybe even some pictures to illustrate it. I have some lovely old photographs that might be just the thing. Let me go dig them out. You know, love, this could be a really great way to explore the different family styles we've had over the years. You know, with me and your dad being separated, and then me meeting your step-dad... it's all been a bit complicated, but it's made our family so rich and interesting.

Ah'm tellin' thee, I'm fair exhausted after that shift at t'library yesterday. Been on me feet all day, wi' nowt but a few breaks in between. How were yer lectures, then? Yeah, they were alright, I s'pose. Had a bit of a group project meeting, and we're getting on alright with it, I think. But, you know, it's always a bit of a struggle gettin' everyone to agree on things. How's yer coursework comin' along, anyway? Oh, it's comin' along, slowly but surely. Ah've been puttin' in some extra hours at t'library, tryin' to get me head around this one essay that's due soon. But, you know, it's hard when all ah can think about is gettin' home and havin' a cuppa. Speakin' of which, have yer seen that new razor they've got out? The one wi' all the fancy blades and whatnot? Actually, yeah, I saw it advertised online the other day. I was thinkin' of gettin' it, 'cause I'm gettin' a bit sick of me old one. It's always leavin' me with razor burn and ingrown hairs. Do you think it's worth the money, though? Ah don't know, but ah'm tempted to give it a go. Ah mean, anyfing's better than shavin' wi' a rusty old blade, int it? And ah've 'eard it's really good for gettin' rid of them pesky hairs on yer bikini line. Ah'm fair sick of waxin', to be honest wi' thee. It's just too much 'assle. Totally agree with you there. Waxin's just too painful, and it's always so expensive. And don't even get me started on epilators – ah mean, what even is the point of those? Just a bunch of unnecessary pain, if you ask me. Shavin's just so much easier, even if it doesn't last as long. Exactly! And another thing, ah've been thinkin' about just embracin' me body hair, like some of t'lads do. Ah mean, it's just a natural part of bein' human, int it? But, at t'same time, ah don't know if ah could pull it off. Ah've always been a bit self-conscious about me hairy legs, especially in t'summer. Yeah, I know what you mean. Ah've always been a bit embarrassed about me armpit hair, but at the same time, it's just so much easier to not shave it all the time.

Alrigh' pet, how's it goin'? Been a long week, an' I'm made up to be 'ere wi' ye, havin' a pint down at the pub. I was just readin' about the history o' alphabets, an' it's fascinatin' how they've evolved ower time. Did ye know the Latin alphabet's the basis fer most alphabets used today? Ah, yeah! I've always been interested in that sorta thing. The way languages an' writing systems 'ave developed is really intriguing. An' speakin' o' development, 'ave you 'eard about the new craft beer they're servin' 'ere? I've been meanin' to try it out. What do you reckon, shall we give it a go? Aye, why not? I'm game fer tryin' new things, especially when it comes to beer. But, ye know, it's funny... I was talkin' to this mate o' mine, an' 'e was sayin' 'ow 'e's cut down on drinkin' a lot lately. 'E's more into fitness an' that, an' 'e says it's made a right big difference. I'm thinkin' o' doin' the same, but it's 'ard when ye enjoy a pint as much as I do! Yeah, I can understand that. I've been tryin' to cut down meself, but it's difficult when ye're in a social environment like this. Everyone's 'avin' a laugh, an' it feels like ye're missin' out if ye don't join in. But, on a different note, 'ave you 'eard about the recent boxin' match between Tyson Fury an' Deontay Wilder? It was a right intense fight, an' I was on the edge o' me seat the whole time! Aye, I did catch that one! Fury's a genius in the ring, int 'e? An' it's amazin' 'ow 'e's overcome all the struggles 'e's faced, especially wi' 'is mental 'ealth. It just goes to show that wi' the right mindset, ye can achieve anythin' ye set yer mind to. An' speakin' o' struggles, 'ave ye seen the news about the racism in football lately? It's disgusting, an' it's somethin' that needs to be addressed ASAP. Yeah, it's a right shame, innit? Football's supposed to be a beautiful game, but the racism an' prejudice that's still prevalent in it is just appalling. I mean, we're in the 21st century, an' ye'd think we'd 'ave moved past all that by now.

I'm telling you, Sarah, this renovation project for the old town hall is going to be a challenge. The historical significance of the building is immense, and we need to make sure we do it justice. I've been researching similar projects, and I think we should consider applying for funding from the Heritage Lottery Fund. Ah, yes, I agree, Emily. The town hall is a gem, and it's essential we preserve its character. I've worked with the Heritage Lottery Fund before, and I can tell you, it's not an easy process. We'll need to submit a watertight bid, complete with a comprehensive business plan and a detailed budget. Have you given any thought to how we'll structure our proposal? Well, I was thinking we could emphasize the community benefits of the project. The town hall has been a hub of activity for generations, and restoring it to its former glory will not only preserve a piece of history but also provide a much-needed community space. I've spoken to some of the local residents, and they're all very keen to see the project happen. That's a great angle to take, Emily. Community engagement is always a key factor in these types of projects. I've seen it time and time again – when local people are invested in a project, it's much more likely to succeed. Now, let's talk about the nitty-gritty of the business plan. We'll need to demonstrate that our proposal is financially viable and that we have a clear plan for the ongoing maintenance and management of the building. Absolutely. I've been looking into that, and I think we should consider setting up a trust or a charity to oversee the project. That way, we can ensure that the building is protected for future generations and that any profits are reinvested in the community. What do you think? I think that's a fantastic idea, Emily. A trust or charity would provide a level of accountability and transparency, which is essential when dealing with public funds. I've worked with a similar organization in the past, and it's been incredibly successful. Now, let me tell you a story – I was involved in a project to restore a historic church in Buckinghamshire, and we set up a trust to manage the funds. It was a huge success, and the church is now thriving.

Alrigh' pet, how's it goin'? I've been meanin' to ask ye about yer research. How's the PhD comin' along, then? Ah, it's going alright, I suppose. Just trying to get this paper finished for the conference next month. You know how it is. I'm looking at the sociolinguistic aspects of dialect variation in the Midlands. Aye, that sounds fascinatin'! I've always been interested in how language varies across different regions. I did a bit of research on the Geordie dialect during me postgrad, ye know. It's amazin' how much it differs from standard English. Yeah, I can imagine. I've been noticing that even within the Midlands, there are distinct differences in pronunciation and vocabulary. It's really interesting to explore. And speaking of interesting, have you thought about where we want to go for our holiday this year? Ooh, now that ye mention it, I've been thinkin' about that a lot lately! I was thinkin' maybe somewhere in Europe, like France or Spain. Somewhere with a bit of culture and nice weather. What do ye think, pet? That sounds great, actually. I've always wanted to visit Barcelona. The architecture, the food... and of course, the language. I've been tryin' to learn a bit of Catalan, but it's not easy, let me tell you. Ah, Catalan, that's a tough one! But I'm sure ye'll pick it up in no time, bein' the clever lad ye are. And yeah, Barcelona's a great choice. We can explore the city, visit all the famous landmarks... and I can practice me Spanish, ha! Exactly! And we can also look into the linguistics of the region, see how Catalan and Spanish intersect. It'll be a great opportunity for us to learn something new together. Sounds like a plan, pet! Now, shall we get the tea ready? I'm gaspin' for a cuppa. What kind of tea do ye fancy? We've got English breakfast, Earl Grey... Ah, just a normal brew for me, thanks. And by the way, I've been meanin' to ask you, have you come across any interesting research on language acquisition lately? Actually, yes! I was readin' about this study on bilingual children and how they develop their language skills. It's really interestin' to see how their brains process multiple languages at such a young age.

Alright kids, how was your day at school? Did you enjoy your lunch today? Yeah, it was okay. We had pizza and vegetables. But I didn't like the vegetables, Mummy. That's alright, sweetie. You don't have to eat everything on your plate. But try to have a little bit of vegetables every day, they're good for you. I ate all my vegetables, Mummy! And I liked the pizza too. Well done, darling! I'm proud of you. You know, when I was at school, we used to have really nice school dinners. We even had dessert sometimes. Really, Mummy? What kind of dessert did you have? Oh, we had all sorts of things like apple crumble, treacle tart, and even ice cream on special occasions. Ooh, I love ice cream! Can we have ice cream tonight, Mummy? Not tonight, darling. But maybe we can have some at Granny's house this weekend. She's making your favorite dinner, isn't she? Yeah! Granny's making chicken nuggets and chips. And we're going to play games and watch a movie. That sounds like so much fun. Don't forget, I need to give you some money for school tomorrow. I'm telling you, that film we saw last night was so thought-provoking. The way it portrayed the historical events was fascinating. It really made me think about how we teach history in schools. It's all about ticking boxes and meeting targets, rather than actually educating the students. I think we need to take a step back and look at the bigger picture. What do we want our students to achieve? What kind of society do we want to create? If we can answer those questions, then we can start building an education system that truly prepares students for the future. You know, when I was at school, we didn't have all these fancy qualifications and assessments. We just learned because we wanted to, and it seemed to work just fine. I'm not saying it was perfect, but there was a sense of curiosity and love for learning that seems to be missing nowadays. That's an interesting point. I think we've lost sight of the joy of learning in our pursuit of academic achievement. As a teacher, I try to create a sense of wonder and curiosity in my students, but it's not always easy.

I'm tellin' ya, the weather's been proper dodgy lately, ain't it? Reminds me of them days during the war, when the skies were always grey and the rain never seemed to stop. I'm going to miss this route, you know? Driving from Mum's to your place has become a routine for me over the years. It's hard to believe we're doing it for the last time before I move. I know, son. Alright, love, I think we've finalized the menu for your grandmother's birthday dinner. We've got the starter, main course, and dessert all sorted. What do you think about the seating arrangements? That's a good idea. I was thinking we could also make some little name cards for the tables so she can remember who everyone is. And maybe we can even make a little schedule for the day so she knows what's happening when.

Ey up, how's it goin'? I'm dyin' for a cuppa. This French coffee's not doin' it for me, y'know? I know what you mean! We've got a big garden and everythin', so I'm lookin' forward to havin' a few barbecues and that. That sounds ace! I'm a bit jealous, to be honest. I'm still undecided about where I'm goin' to live. I've been lookin' at a few places, but nothin's really standin' out yet. Do you think you'll be havin' a housewarming party or anythin'? Definitely! We'll have to sort sommat out, won't we? Alright kids, who's excited for Chinese New Year? We're going to make some delicious lactose-free cakes and cookies to celebrate. I am! I am! Mum, I'm so glad you're home. I had the craziest day at school today. I'm still fuming about the proposal to build those wind turbines in our rural area. It's just not suitable, if you ask me. I mean, have you seen the landscape around here? I've been doing some research, and it's astonishing how much money the government is pouring into subsidies for alternative energy sources, while neglecting the need for research into new technologies. I mean, I'm all for reducing our carbon footprint, but not at the expense of our countryside. There must be better ways to do it.

I'm telling you, learning to drive isn't as easy as it used to be. I remember when I first got behind the wheel, it was a breeze. Dad, how's it going? I'm so glad we're having lunch together today. I feel like I haven't seen you in ages. Ah, lovely to see you too, dear. I'm doing all right, considering. I'm telling you, mate, I had the most absurd conversation with my lit professor the other day. Ah'm tellin' thee, it's been a mad week at work. We've 'ad a conference every day, an' I'm fair knackered. How's life as a labourer treatin' yer, then, lad? It's been alright, I s'pose. Alright, love, can you hear me now? I've got the Skype working, and I'm showing you around the garden. You can see the blooming flowers, and the new fence the neighbours put up. Ah'm tellin' thee, t'birds are singing their hearts out this time of year. I were out in t'garden yesterday, and I could 'ear all sorts of different songs. Hi, how are you doing today? I saw you ushering in court earlier. How was your day? Oh, hello! I'm doing all right, thanks for asking. Just trying to keep everything in order, you know how it is. Wow, that's really cool. I had no idea. I've always been interested in history, and it's amazing to think about how it can still be seen in the way we speak today. Exactly! And it's not just limited to the northeast, either. Different parts of the country have their own unique linguistic histories and influences. It's really fascinating to explore and learn about. I can imagine. I've been thinkin' about doin' some travelin' around the UK, just to experience different parts of the country and hear the different accents and dialects firsthand. Have you got any recommendations for places to visit? Oh, definitely.

Blimey, I'm tellin' ya, this weather's been dreadful, ain't it? All this rain's playin' havoc with me joints. Me knees are killin' me, they are. Oh, I know what you mean, dear. Hey girls, it's so great to finally catch up with you all. I feel like it's been ages since we've all been in the same room together. How's everyone doing? I'm doing fantastic, thanks for asking. Just got back from a lovely weekend in the countryside with my boyfriend. We're actually thinking of getting married soon, so that's all very exciting. Oh my god, congratulations! I've already started thinking about the diet I'll need to go on before the big day. Ugh, don't even get me started on diets. I've been trying to lose weight for ages, but it's just not happening.

Ah, nice cuppa, ANON. You always knew how to make a good brew. I'm still trying to figure out this new smartphone my granddaughter got me. All these apps and whatnot, it's a bit bewildering. Oh, I know what you mean, dear. I had to get my son to set up my tablet for me. I just use it for email and Facebook, but it's still a bit of a mystery. I do love looking at all the pictures of the children on it, though. Yes, technology can be overwhelming at times. I've been trying to get my students to use more educational apps in the classroom, but it's an uphill battle. They're more interested in playing games on their phones than learning, unfortunately. Games, you say? I used to love playing chess and bridge when I was younger. Nowadays, it's all about these video games, isn't it? My grandson is always talking about Fortnite and Minecraft. I have no idea what it's all about. Oh, I've heard of Minecraft! My niece's children love playing it. They're always building things and going on adventures. I've even tried playing it with them a few times, but I'm afraid I'm not very good at it. Yes, Minecraft is very popular among children. I've even used it in my teaching to help them learn about geometry and spatial awareness. But, I have to say, it's not just children who enjoy playing games. I've been known to play a game or two of Scrabble in my free time. Scrabble, now that's a game I can get behind! I used to play it with my wife all the time. We'd have these lovely afternoons, just the two of us, playing games and drinking tea. She was always better at it than me, though. That sounds lovely, dear. I'm sure she's still with you in spirit. Speaking of which, have you heard from your granddaughter lately? How's she doing with her horse riding? Ah, yes! She's doing wonderfully. She's been competing in all these shows and events. I'm so proud of her. You know, I used to love horses when I was younger. I even had a pony of my own, briefly. But, alas, we couldn't afford to keep it.

Ah, it's so lovely to finally catch up with you, John. I feel like it's been ages since we last had a chance to chat. How have you been keeping? I've been doing all right, thank you for asking, Emily. Just enjoying my retirement and trying to stay busy. I've taken up gardening, you know. It's a great way to get some exercise and fresh air. Gardening, how wonderful! I've always been fascinated by it, but I don't have much of a green thumb, I'm afraid. I do love language, though, and I've been thinking of starting a new course to learn Spanish. Have you ever had any experience with languages, John? Well, I did learn some French at school, but that's about it, I'm afraid. I never really had the chance to use it much in my line of work, but I do think it's a valuable skill to have. My granddaughter is actually learning Spanish in school, and she's really enjoying it. That's great to hear! I think it's so important for children to learn languages from a young age. It really opens up their possibilities for travel and work in the future. Speaking of travel, have you and your wife been on any exciting trips lately? Actually, we did go to France last year, and it was lovely. We visited some of the wine regions and sampled some of the local cuisine. It was a real treat. We're thinking of going to Italy next year, maybe to Tuscany. Have you ever been to Italy, Emily? Yes, I have! I went to Rome and Florence a few years ago, and it was just incredible. The history, the art, the food... everything was just so amazing. I would love to go back and explore more of the country. What made you decide on Tuscany? Well, we've heard great things about the scenery and the wine, and we're both big fans of Italian food. Plus, it seems like a relatively relaxed pace of life, which suits us just fine at our age. We're not as energetic as we used to be, after all! I can understand that. I've been feeling a bit worn out myself lately, what with work and trying to plan some weekend trips. Do you have any fun plans for the weekend, John?

Blimey, I'm so glad it's Friday, ain't you, mate? Valentine's Day and all that. How was yours, then? Ah, it were alright, I s'pose. Didn't do much, just went to the cinema with me mates. We watched that new rom-com. You know, the one with Emma Stone? Ooh, yeah! I've been meanin' to see that. How was it, then? Was it any good? It were okay, I reckon. Had some funny bits, but it were a bit cheesy in some places. You'd probably like it, though. You're a sucker for them romantic films, ain't ya? Shut it, you! I am not! Anyway, after the cinema, what did you lot get up to? Did you go for some grub somewhere? Yeah, we went to that new Italian place downtown. The food were lovely, but the service were a bit slow. I were gettin' proper hangry by the time me pasta arrived! Oh, I feel you! Nothin' worse than waitin' for food when you're starvin'! Did you try their pizza? I've been hearin' good things about it. Nah, I didn't, but me mate did. She said it were alright, but not as good as the one from that new place in Camden. You know, the one with the weird name? Oh, you mean Bella's? I've been meanin' to try that out. Is it any good, then? Yeah, it's supposed to be. Me mate said the owner's got a right funny accent, though. Sounds like a proper cockney, but apparently, he's from up north or somethin'! That's nothin'! I've got a mate who's from the Philippines, but she's got a proper Brummie accent now. It's hilarious! Yeah, accents are funny, ain't they? I've got a mate who's from London, but she's been livin' in the Midlands for so long now, she's started soundin' like a local! Yeah, it's crazy how that happens, innit? Anyway, enough about accents. What's your plans for the weekend, then? Got anythin' excitin' lined up? Nah, not really. Just gonna do some shoppin' on Saturday, maybe catch up on some coursework. You know, the usual. How about you? Same here, mate. Got a lot of work to do, but I'm thinkin' of goin' to the market on Sunday.

I'm telling you, the recent rise in racism in politics is just appalling. It's like we're taking steps backwards. I was reading this article about how certain politicians are using dog-whistle tactics to stir up hatred towards immigrants. I know, it's disgusting. And it's not just limited to the UK, it's a global problem. I've been writing about it for my blog, and the more I research, the more I realize how deep-seated the issue is. What's even more worrying is how it's affecting people's daily lives, like the housing market for instance. Exactly! The housing market is a perfect example. I mean, have you seen the prices of flats in London lately? It's like they're intentionally pricing out certain communities. I've been working on a project to design affordable housing, but it's an uphill battle. The council keeps rejecting our proposals, saying they're not "economically viable". That's frustrating. I've been trying to get a foot on the property ladder for ages, but it's impossible. I've been looking at shared ownership schemes, but they're not much better. It's like the system is designed to keep people like us renting forever. And it's not just about the money, it's about the lack of security. I mean, I'm a freelance journalist, I don't have a stable income, so I'm always worried about being evicted. I feel you. As an architect, I've seen how the housing market is driven by profit rather than people's needs. It's all about making a quick buck, rather than creating sustainable communities. And it's not just about the buildings themselves, it's about the impact they have on the environment and the people who live in them. I've been trying to convince my firm to take on more projects that prioritize social and environmental sustainability, but it's an uphill battle. I can imagine. It's the same with journalism. Sometimes I feel like I'm just scratching the surface of the real issues, because the people in power don't want to rock the boat. But I'm trying to use my platform to amplify the voices of people who are affected by these policies. Like, have you heard about the new development that's going up in Hackney?

I'm getting a bit anxious about the baby starting nursery next week. I know it's a big step for both of us, but I'm not sure if I'm ready to leave her with strangers all day. Ah, mum, don't worry! You've been preparing for this moment for months. The baby will be fine, and it'll be good for you to get back to work and have some adult conversation. You can't stay at home forever, can you? I know, I know. It's just hard to imagine not being with her all the time. And what if she doesn't eat her lunch or takes a nap on time? I've got all these worries going around in my head. Mum, the nursery staff are trained professionals. They'll take good care of her, and they'll make sure she eats and sleeps properly. Besides, it's not like you're abandoning her. You'll be dropping her off and picking her up every day. You'll still get to spend plenty of time with her. I suppose you're right. It's just that being a mum is such a big responsibility, and I don't want to mess anything up. And to make matters worse, I've got to start thinking about weaning her off breast milk soon. Have you any idea how complicated that process is? Actually, I've been reading up on it a bit, and it seems like it's not too bad. You just need to introduce some solid foods gradually and see how she takes to them. And don't worry if it takes a few tries to get it right – every baby is different. That's true, I suppose. I just want to do what's best for her. Anyway, enough about the baby for now. What about you? How's university going? Are you enjoying your courses this semester? Yeah, it's going all right, I suppose. Some of the lectures are a bit dry, but I'm managing to keep up with the workload. And I've been thinking about our next family holiday – maybe we could go to Spain or Italy sometime soon? That sounds like a lovely idea! I've always wanted to visit Italy. We should start looking into it and booking something for next summer. And speaking of summer, have you seen any good TV shows lately?

I'm so glad we're all finally sitting down together, I feel like I haven't seen anyone all day. How was everyone's day, then? It was alright, I suppose. I had a meeting with a potential donor for the charity, so that was a positive note. But I have to say, I'm a bit worried about this statement I have to give to the police tomorrow. I've never been very good at dealing with that sort of thing. Oh, don't worry, Dad. You'll be fine. Just tell them what happened and answer their questions honestly. What's it about again? It's about the incident at the charity event last week. Someone reported that one of our volunteers had been acting suspiciously, and the police want to know if I noticed anything unusual. That sounds like a right hassle. But I'm sure you'll get through it, love. You're always so calm and collected. By the way, has anyone seen the latest EE phone bill? I could've sworn I left it right here on the table. I think I saw it in the living room, Mum. I'll go grab it for you. Ah, yeah, here it is. Blimey, our phone bill is massive this month! What's going on? I know, I was just about to say that. I think it's because of all the international calls your dad made for work. And maybe some of the data usage from our holiday last month. Ah, yes, that's probably it. I did make a few calls to the States, didn't I? And how was your day, son? How's the business going? It's going well, thanks. We've been getting a lot of new clients lately, so that's keeping us busy. But I'm a bit stressed about meeting our quarterly targets. We need to come up with some new strategies to stay ahead of the competition. Yeah, I know how you feel. We've been having some issues at the store too. Our sales have been down lately, and I'm not sure what to do about it. Well, maybe we can all brainstorm some ideas together after dinner. Sometimes talking through problems with others can help you come up with solutions you wouldn't have thought of on your own. That's a great idea, love.

Mate, it's been ages! Congratulations on the marriage. How's life been treating you? I feel like we haven't caught up in years. Thanks, buddy! Life's been good. Just got back from the honeymoon and settling into married life. You know how it is. We've been meaning to have you over for dinner, but we've been so busy with the new place and all. I can imagine. I've been keeping busy myself with work and whatnot. I've been meaning to ask, have you been watching any good TV shows lately? I just finished binge-watching Spartacus and I'm looking for something new to get into. Actually, yeah! I've been watching this documentary series on Roman history. It's really interesting. I never knew how much of an impact they had on modern society. And speaking of impact, have you tried that new Italian place downtown? Their pasta is to die for. Roman history, eh? I've always been fascinated by that era. And yeah, I've tried the Italian place. Their carbonara is amazing. But anyway, back to Spartacus – what did you think of the show? I loved the first season, but it started to go downhill after that. Yeah, I agree. The first season was intense. But I think the problem was that they killed off too many good characters too early. I mean, who kills off the main villain in the first season? It's like they didn't plan ahead or something. Exactly! And it's not just Spartacus. I've been noticing that a lot of shows are killing off main characters way too early. It's like they're trying to be edgy or something. I was listening to this musician the other day, and he was talking about how he got his inspiration from ancient history. It's crazy how much of an impact it still has on art and media today. That's really cool. I've always been fascinated by how different art forms can draw inspiration from the same sources. By the way, have you tried that new tea shop that just opened up? I heard they have some amazing herbal blends. Actually, yeah! I went there last week and got this amazing mortar and pestle to make my own teas at home. It's been a game-changer. I've been experimenting with all sorts of herbs and spices.

Hey, how was your week at school? I felt like it dragged on forever. I'm so glad it's the weekend now. I know, right? I'm exhausted. We had that huge English test on Wednesday, and I'm still trying to process how I did. How about you, did you find it tough? Yeah, it was alright, I suppose. I mean, I studied pretty hard for it, but there were a few questions that caught me off guard. I'm a bit worried about my grade, to be honest. But hey, at least we have the school orchestra to look forward to, right? I've been practicing my flute like crazy. Oh, totally! The orchestra is always a highlight of my week. I love playing with everyone. Have you heard that Mr. Johnson is thinking of changing the set list for the upcoming concert? I heard we might be playing some more modern pieces, which could be really cool. Really? That sounds amazing! I love playing the more contemporary stuff. It's so much more fun than the classical pieces we usually do. Do you think we'll have to audition for the solo parts again? I'm not sure, but I hope so. I've been working on this one piece that I think would be perfect for a solo. Speaking of which, have you seen the new art project that Mr. Thompson assigned in art class? It looks like it's going to be a real challenge. Ugh, don't even get me started on art class. I'm really struggling to come up with ideas for the project. I wish we could just do something simple for once. And to make matters worse, I have French lessons right after art, and Madame Dupont is being super strict about our pronunciation. I feel you. I'm not exactly proficient in French either. But hey, at least we have each other to suffer through it with. By the way, have you talked to Emily lately? I haven't seen her around much, and I'm starting to get a bit worried. Actually, I saw her at lunch yesterday, and she seemed fine. I think she's just been really busy with her own schoolwork and extracurriculars. But we should definitely check in with her soon and make sure everything is okay. Yeah, that's a good idea. We should invite her over for a study session or something.

Ah'm so glad we're havin' a catch-up, pet. How's school goin', lad? Are yer enjoyin' yer lessons? Aye, it's alrigh', miss. I've been doin' alright in me exams, but I'm strugglin' a bit wi' me maths. Me mam's been helpin' me out, though. That's great, lad! Yer mam's always been good at maths, hasn't she? I remember when we were at school, she was always top of the class. Anyway, how's yer accent comin' along? Yer sound more like a Geordie every time I see yer! Ah know, miss! Me mates at school always say ah sound like a proper Newcastle lad now. But ah've been tryin' to keep a bit of me Darlington accent, y'knaa? Ah, hello, love! Sorry ah'm late. Ah got held up at the hospital, visitin' me sister. She's not been well lately. Oh, sorry to hear that, Brenda. How's she doin'? Is she gettin' the right treatment? Yeah, she is, thanks for askin'. The doctors and nurses at the hospital have been great. Ah was just talkin' to one of the nurses, and she was sayin' how hard it is to get funding for some of the treatments. It's a shame, really, because ah think it's essential for people's wellness. That's true, miss. Ah've been learnin' about statistics in school, and it's amazin' how much of a difference proper funding can make. Ah mean, did yer know that... Oh, lad, don't get too caught up in yer statistics just yet! Let's enjoy our coffee and chat about sommat more interestin'. Brenda, have yer heard about the new food festival that's comin' to Darlington? Ah heard it's goin' to be a great event. Ooh, no, ah hadn't! Ah love tryin' new foods, especially if they're locally sourced. Ah might have to come along and check it out. Are yer goin', lad? Aye, ah am! Me mam's takin' me and me mates. We're all excited to try some of the different foods and drinks. And ah heard there's goin' to be a big screen showin' the football match, so we can watch that too. That sounds like a great day out! Ah might have to join yer, lad. Ah love watchin' the football, especially when the Boro are playin'. Ah, and speakin' of sport, have yer seen the new branding for the team?

I'm telling you, it's getting more and more difficult to drive in this city. The traffic is terrible, and people just don't seem to care about following the rules of the road anymore. I was on my way home from work the other day, and I saw someone running a red light. It's just ridiculous. Ah, come on, love. You can't blame the drivers entirely. The roads are getting more congested, and it's not just the cars. There are cyclists and pedestrians everywhere. It's a miracle nobody gets hurt. By the way, can you pass the mashed potatoes, please? I think it's all about self-control, dear. If people just followed the rules and were more considerate of others, we wouldn't have half the problems we do. And it's not just driving. I mean, have you seen the state of some people? Obesity is a huge issue, and it's all because people can't control themselves when it comes to food. That's a bit harsh, isn't it? I mean, obesity is a complex issue, and it's not just about self-control. There are genetic factors at play, as well as environmental and socio-economic factors. We can't just blame the individual. But that's just it, isn't it? We do tend to blame the individual. And it's not just with obesity. We blame people for their circumstances, rather than looking at the bigger picture. Like with religion, for example. Some people are born into a certain faith, and they're expected to follow it without question. It's not always a choice, is it? I never thought about it that way, but I suppose you're right. We do tend to judge people based on their circumstances. But what about genes, then? Don't they play a role in shaping who we are and what we do? Oh, absolutely. I mean, look at our family. We all have similar traits and characteristics. It's like we're puzzle pieces, and the genes are the bits that fit together to make us who we are. Speaking of puzzles, has anyone done that new jigsaw that I got? Actually, I started it the other day, but I had to stop because I got a bit of a headache. I think it's because of the new carpet we got.

I'm telling you, I've been struggling to get my students to engage with the new Moodle platform. I've set up all the modules and assignments, but they just don't seem to be accessing the material. Ah, come on, it's not that complicated. You just need to make sure you've enabled the correct permissions and that the students know how to navigate the site. Why don't we sit down and go through it together? I can show you some of the features I've used in my own modules, and we can work out a plan for your students. That would be brilliant, thanks. I feel like I'm just not reaching them like I used to. And with the new semester starting soon, I want to make sure I'm prepared. I've been using the analytics tool to track my students' activity, and it's been really helpful in identifying areas where they're struggling. We can set that up for your modules as well, and I can show you how to interpret the data. That sounds amazing. I had no idea it could do all that. I feel like I've been teaching the same way for years, and it's time for a bit of a shake-up. Do you think we could also look at incorporating some more interactive elements, like quizzes and discussions? Absolutely. Moodle has some great tools for creating interactive content. We can set up some quizzes and forums, and I can show you how to grade and moderate them. And if you want to get really fancy, we could even look at using some of the more advanced features, like peer review and self-assessment. Wow, you're a genius. I don't know what I'd do without you.

I'm so glad we're finally having a chance to relax at home. I feel like we've been on the go non-stop since we got back from our trip to the States. I know what you mean. I'm still feeling the effects of jetlag, to be honest. It's taking me a while to adjust to the time difference. Yeah, I'm the same. I keep waking up in the middle of the night thinking it's morning. But anyway, enough about that. Have you given any more thought to going to see that play at the local theatre? Actually, I was thinking about it earlier today. I checked the schedule and it looks like they have a few performances left before it closes. What do you think about going next Friday? That sounds perfect. I've heard great things about the production and I'd love to see it. Shall we book the tickets online or try to get them at the box office? I think it's safer to book them online, just in case they sell out. I can do it now if you'd like. That would be great, thanks. And while you're doing that, I was thinking... have you seen our friends' new baby photos on social media? Yeah, I saw them earlier. They're adorable, aren't they? I was thinking we should arrange to visit them soon and meet the little one in person. Absolutely. I've been meaning to give them a call and arrange something. Maybe we could take them out for a meal or something? That's a good idea. Or we could just go over to their place and bring some food with us. I'm sure they'd appreciate the company and the break from cooking. Yeah, that sounds like a plan. I'll give them a call and see what they think. Oh, and by the way, how did your lecture go today? It was fine, thanks. Just a standard lecture on 19th-century literature. Nothing too out of the ordinary. How about you? How was your day? It was good, thanks. I had a meeting with some colleagues to discuss our upcoming research project, and then I had a few hours of lecturing. Nothing too exciting, but it was productive. Sounds like you had a busy day. I'm glad we can just relax now and enjoy each other's company.

Lah, it's great to 'ave you over for a cuppa, mate. I've been meanin' to ask, how's your family doin' back in Kurdistan? I've always been fascinated by the culture and history of the region. Ah, thank you for having me, it's a pleasure to be here. My family is doing well, alhamdulillah. But it's not easy, you know, with the situation in Iraq and all the bureaucracy. My cousin is actually tryin' to get a visa to come to the UK, but it's a nightmare. Have you ever had to deal with that sort of thing? Aye, I've had me share of dealin's with visas and whatnot. I've got a mate who's a lecturer in Libya, and he's always complainin' about the politics of oil and how it's affectin' the country. It's a right mess, if you ask me. And now with the Wahabi influence spreadin' across the region, it's gettin' even more complicated. Yes, it's a very sensitive topic. The Wahabi ideology is a big problem, not just in Libya but in many other countries as well. And it's not just about religion, it's about politics and power. I've seen it firsthand, workin' as an interpreter and translator, and it's heartbreaking to see young people gettin' caught up in it. That's a good point, mate. Young people are the future, and they need to be educated about the dangers of extremism. I've got a few students from Libya and Iraq in me classes, and they're always eager to learn and share their perspectives. It's refreshin' to see. Absolutely. Education is key. And it's not just about book learnin', it's about exposure to different cultures and ideas. I've been thinkin' of movin' to a new house, actually, to a more diverse area where me kids can grow up with people from different backgrounds. Ah, that's a great idea, mate! I've been thinkin' of movin' too, now that me kids are grown up and moved out. Maybe we can even look for a new place together, eh? I've got a mate who's a real estate agent, and he's always lookin' for new clients. Ha! That would be great, thanks for the offer. But I think I'll need to get me cousin's visa sorted out first, then we can start thinkin' about movin' house.

I'm so glad we decided to have a roast lamb for dinner tonight, it's been ages since we've had one. And I must say, it's turned out perfectly. Absolutely, the flavors are just right. You know, I was thinking, maybe we should consider putting a TV in the dining room. It would be nice to watch a bit of telly while we eat, especially on special occasions. Oh, I'm not sure about that, dear. I think it's nice to have some time without the distraction of the TV. We can just enjoy each other's company and conversation. I see what you both mean. Alright kids, gather 'round. I'm planning a fun lesson for my class this week and I need your help. Well, it's like a birthday, but it's six months after your actual birthday. It's just a fun way to celebrate the halfway point until your next birthday. Ooh, can we have a half-birthday party at home too? We'll see, okay? Now, I need to make a list of everything I need for the lesson. Can you both help me with that? Yeah! I wanna help! We need flour, sugar, eggs... And chocolate chips! Great job, kids! You're both very helpful. Now, I also need to find a book to read to the class. I was thinking of going to Morrisons to see if they have any good ones. Ooh, can we come with you to Morrisons? I love going to the bookstore! Yeah, and can we get some toys too? We'll see, okay? Maybe we can find some toys, but first, let's focus on finding a good book for the lesson. Mummy, I found a great book at school about dragons! You should read that one! Yeah, and I like the one about cars!

I'm telling you, I've been thinking of getting a new car. Mine's been playing up lately and I don't fancy being stuck on the side of the road again. What do you think I should get? Well, what's your budget like? You know I've been looking into electric cars, they seem like the way forward. Plus, they're better for the environment. That's true, I've been considering going electric. But I've also heard they can be a bit pricey. I was thinking maybe a hybrid? I've seen some good deals on those recently. I've seen them online, but I'm not sure I can justify the cost. Maybe one day when I've won the lottery! Ha! By the way, have you been on Facebook lately? I posted some pictures from our last holiday and I was wondering if you'd seen them. Yeah, I saw them. You looked like you were having a great time. I did notice that some of our friends from uni had commented on them, though. I'm starting to think that Facebook is just a way for people to spy on each other's lives now. I know what you mean. It can feel a bit like that sometimes. But at the same time, it's nice to keep in touch with people you might not otherwise see or hear from. And it's great for sharing photos and updates with family who live far away. That's true. I just wish people would use it more responsibly. I mean, have you seen some of the nonsense that gets shared on there? It's like people don't even fact-check anything anymore. Ugh, don't even get me started. I saw something the other day that was just completely made up, but it had been shared by like, a thousand people. It's scary to think about how much misinformation is out there. Exactly! And it's not just Facebook, either. The whole internet can be a bit of a minefield when it comes to finding reliable sources of information. I've been trying to teach my students to be more critical of what they read online, but it's not always easy.

I'm knackered after that shift at work today. I don't know how much more of this sales assistant job I can handle. Five hours on my feet is exhausting. What's wrong, didn't you have a good day? Now, can I get you a snack or something? I'm starving after my shift. Yeah, can I have some popcorn? And can you show me how to use the TV remote? I always get confused with all the buttons. Okay, let me show you. It's pretty simple once you get the hang of it.

Ey up, lad! Fancy a cuppa while we're chattin' about the footy? I've got a fresh pot brewin' in the staff room down the hall. Ah, sounds like a plan, mate! Sounds like a load of waffle to me. But, I do know one thing – I don't trust any of 'em, regardless of the party. They're all just in it for themselves, if you ask me. Now, talkin' about somethin' that really matters... did you see the Liverpool match last weekend? Ah, yeah! I did! We played a blinder, didn't we? Although, I was a bit worried when they scored that equalizer... thought it was gonna be one of those days, you know?

I'm telling you, I've been listening to the most fascinating BNC recordings for work. It's amazing how much you can learn about language patterns just from conversations like this one. Oh, yeah? I've always been interested in language, but I never pursued it academically. I'm more of a creative writer, you know? I've been trying to get more into editing, though. I just started a new job as an editor for a small publishing company. Congratulations! That's amazing. I've been trying to get more into LinkedIn, actually. I feel like it's so important to have a professional online presence, especially in our line of work. Do you have a LinkedIn profile? Yeah, I do. I'm not super active on it, but I try to keep my profile up to date. I've been meaning to connect with you, actually. I'll send you a request later. Hey, guys! What's going on? Although, I have to say, I'm a bit jealous of people who get to travel all the time. I'm scared of flying, which makes it really hard for me to go on long trips. Oh, I'm the same way! I hate flying. But I've been trying to face my fears and travel more.

Blimey, I'm starvin'! How's the pasta comin' along, love? You're the best cook I know, and I'm not just sayin' that 'cause I'm hungry. Oh, it's coming along, dear. We're just gettin' dinner ready. Hello, Alex! Come join the party! Hey, guys! Sorry I'm late. Traffic was a nightmare. What's cookin'? Smells amazing in here.

I'm so glad we're finally catching up, it feels like it's been ages. How was your week, anything exciting happen? It was pretty busy, to be honest. I had a few deadlines to meet at work, but I did manage to squeeze in a bit of shopping on Friday. I got this lovely new top, have a look. Oh, that's really nice! I love the colour.
