Well, I actually found this top at a little boutique in the city centre. They have some really unique pieces, and the owner is always happy to give you style advice. I'll have to take you there next time we're out. That sounds great, thanks for the tip. Now, shall we get started on dinner? I was thinking we could make some pasta with a tomato sauce. Sounds perfect to me. I love a good pasta dish. What kind of tomatoes are you using? I've got some fresh ones from the market, and I was thinking of adding some basil and garlic to give it a bit of flavour. Mmm, that sounds delicious. I've been trying to cook more with fresh ingredients lately. It makes such a difference to the taste, doesn't it? Absolutely. The instructor is really knowledgeable and it's a good way to relax after a long day. You should come with me sometime, I think you'd really enjoy it. I'm telling you, it's been a wild week of teaching here in China. I had a student ask me about the differences between British and American English, and I think I might have confused them more than helped. Ah, I can imagine. Okay, shall we start making plans for that dinner party, then? I'll start looking up recipes and you can send out the invitations. Sounds good to me.

It's so great to finally catch up with you, I feel like it's been ages. How's work been treating you? Still enjoying being a company director? Ah, you know, it's been keeping me busy, as always. But I'm not complaining, it's a challenging role, but rewarding in its own way. How about you, how's the language teaching going? Still inspiring young minds? Yeah, something like that. Actually, I just watched this documentary on Netflix about conspiracy theories, and it was fascinating. I mean, some of the stuff they come up with is just unbelievable, but it's also kind of entertaining. Have you ever looked into any of that? Oh, yeah, I've dabbled in it a bit. I'm like, "Come on, mate, it's been proven time and time again that it's not true!" Yeah, I know what you mean. But at the same time, it's interesting to see how people's minds work, you know? And some of the theories are actually kind of plausible, until you start digging deeper and realize it's all just speculation. But at the same time, you've got to feel for them, being under that much scrutiny all the time.

Ey up, Dad, how much longer till we get to Cornwall? I'm so excited for our holiday! Ah, not too much longer, love. We've just passed Bristol, so we've got a few hours yet. You get to see all the different landscapes and colours. Reminds me of that scene from the Wizard of Oz, when Dorothy lands in Munchkinland and everything is so colourful and vibrant. I'd love to learn more about it. Maybe we can even send each other secret messages while we're on holiday. But first, can we stop for some fuel and get some chocolate? I'm starving! Of course, love.

Ey up, Grandad, how's it goin'? I've just got back from the most amazin' holiday in France. The food was incredible, I'm still dreamin' about the croissants and cheese. Ah, France, beautiful country. I know, it's mental. And have you seen the price of petrol lately? It's like they're tryin' to rob us blind. I'm thinkin' of gettin' an electric car, actually. What do you think, Grandad?

Mum, it's great to be back home. I've missed your cooking so much. What's for lunch? Ah, hello, love! I'm glad you're home safe. I was thinking of making some sandwiches and soup. Ah'm tellin' ye, pet, ah've been meanin' to get some more plants for the livin' room. It's lookin' a bit bare in here, if ye ask me. What do ye think, love? Should we get some more greenery in? I'm so glad we decided to stop for some breakfast before hitting the road again. I don't know about you, but I need something in my stomach before a long drive. Ey up, Sarah, how's it goin'? Been a long day, hasn't it? I'm tellin' yer, I'm proper knackered. Been dealin' with them students all day, and I'm at me wit's end. You know what I don't like? And another thing that gets me goat is when people don't respect the rules. I mean, we've got rules in place for a reason, and if people don't follow 'em, it can cause all sorts of problems.

I'm so glad we decided to meet up here at the café in Brighton, it's been ages since we've all caught up. I had the most hilarious experience last summer when I bumped into some English people abroad. We were all on a package tour in Antwerp, and I swear, it was like being back in England, but with better chocolate. Ah, yes, Antwerp's a great place, I've been there a few times. Oh, don't even get me started on city traffic! I was in London the other day, and it took me over an hour to get from one side of the city to the other. Anyway, speaking of holidays, have you guys thought about where you'd like to go for our next family trip? Maybe somewhere a bit more relaxing, like Dorset? Ooh, that sounds lovely! I've always wanted to go caravanning in Dorset. But, I've been so busy with university and stuff, I haven't had much time to think about it. But, hey, at least I can order a decent cup of coffee in French now! That's great, dear! I've been meaning to ask, how's the retirement treating you? Are you enjoying it? And, by the way, have you seen those cute little puppies that just opened up a shop in Herne Bay? I took the kids there last weekend, and they loved it. Aw, yeah! I've seen them, they're adorable! It's always so hard to find the right gifts, though. Ah, Christmas shopping... it's just not the same since we lost...

Mum, I've been learning about the equality vote in Ireland at school and I just can't believe it was only passed a few years ago. It's mad to think that same-sex marriage wasn't allowed until 2015. I know, love, it's crazy. I remember when it was all over the news. I was so happy when it passed. It's a big step forward for equality. And you know, it's not just about the marriage itself, it's about the rights that come with it. Exactly! We were discussing it in class and some people were saying that it's not fair that it took so long for the vote to happen. But others were saying that at least it happened eventually. What do you think? Well, I think it's a bit of both, to be honest. On one hand, it's great that the vote passed and that same-sex couples now have the same rights as everyone else. But on the other hand, it's ridiculous that it took so long. I mean, love is love, no matter what. You're going to start crying, aren't you, Mum? She's a politician, and she was really interesting. That sounds great! I'm sure you'll make a great politician one day, if that's what you want to do. You're definitely confident enough for it. I was thinking maybe we could invite some friends over and have a game night or something. Oh, that sounds like a great idea! We can definitely organize something. What do you think about having it at home, or should we rent out a venue? Hmm, I think at home would be better. It'll be more relaxed and we can just have a chill night in.

I'm tellin' ya, I had the most interestin' conversation with me mate Dave the other day. He's got this old lathe in 'is workshop, and 'e was showin' me all the different tools 'e uses. I never knew there were so many types of chisels and gouges. Oh, that sounds fascinatin'! I've always been interested in woodwork, but I never had the chance to learn. I'm sure Dave's been doin' it for years to get as good as 'e is. By the way, would anyone like another sandwich? I made a few extra. Oh, thank you, dear! I'll 'ave another one, please. Actually, I tried it out last weekend, and it was quite good! The secret's in the marinade, apparently. You've got to let it sit for at least 24 hours before you roast it. Ooh, that sounds delicious! I'll 'ave to give it a try. You know, it reminds me of that time our niece tried to cook a hamster in the microwave. Oh, blimey! I remember that! She was only little, of course, but still... what was she thinkin'? I think she just wanted to see what would 'appen! Kids can be a bit... unpredictable, can't they? Unpredictable's one word for it! Anyway, where was I? Ah yes, the recipe. I'll 'ave to get it from you, John. I'm always up for tryin' new things in the kitchen. Course, dear! I'll write it down for you. Now, where's that bit of paper...? I'll get some paper and a pen from the other room, shall I?

I'm telling you, I saw the most fascinating thing on the news the other day. A cat got stuck in a tree and the whole town came out to rescue it. I mean, can you imagine? Ah, that's brilliant. I love a good cat story. But you know what's not so brilliant? The state of our banks at the moment. I've been trying to sort out our finances and it's a nightmare. All these hidden fees and charges... it's like they're just waiting for us to slip up so they can pounce. Oh, don't even get me started on banks. I've been dealing with them for years, and it's always the same story. They're only looking out for themselves, not their customers. And have you seen the latest on house prices? It's absurd. Young people these days will never be able to afford their own homes. That's so true. I was talking to a friend the other day and she was saying how she and her husband are struggling to make ends meet. They're married, but they're not even sure if they can afford to start a family. It's heartbreaking. Yeah, and it's not just the cost of living that's the problem. It's the debt that people are accumulating. I mean, I know we've been lucky, but I've seen friends who are struggling to pay off their credit cards and loans. It's a vicious cycle. Well, I think it's all about being responsible with your finances. When I was younger, we didn't have all these credit cards and loans. We had to budget and make do with what we had. And you know what? We were happier for it. That's a good point. Although, I have to say, I do love a good challenge. Like those cryptic crosswords in the newspaper. Have you tried them? Oh, yes. I've tried them, but I'm afraid I'm not very good at them. I prefer something a bit more... straightforward. Like a good old-fashioned crossword. Ah, but that's the beauty of cryptic crosswords. They're like a puzzle, a game. You have to think outside the box and use your imagination. Exactly! And speaking of technology, have you seen those new smartwatches that are out?

Alright, guys, I think it's time for a break from the screens, don't you? You've both been playing on your tablets for hours. Why don't we find a book to read together instead? But, Mummy, I was right in the middle of building a new Lego Ninjago world in Minecraft! I have to finish it. Yeah! And I was helping her! We have to save Jay from the evil forces of the Overlord. I understand that it's exciting, but too much screen time isn't good for you. You need to rest your eyes and use your imagination in different ways. Reading is a great way to do that. Plus, it's good for your learning and vocabulary. But, Mummy, I am using my imagination! I'm building a whole world with Lego and fighting bad guys. It's just like the stories we read, but I get to be in charge of the adventure. And we can make the characters do whatever we want! Like, last time, we made Cole ride a dragon. I see what you mean, and it does sound like fun. However, there's a difference between creating your own stories and playing games, even if they are creative games like Minecraft. When you read, you're experiencing someone else's imagination and learning from their ideas and perspectives. It broadens your understanding of the world. I suppose that makes sense. But can we finish this one thing we're doing? Please? It won't take long, I promise. Yeah, please? We're almost done saving Jay. Alright, alright. You can finish what you're doing, but then we're going to take a break and find a book. Maybe we can even find one about adventures or superheroes that you'll enjoy. Thanks, Mummy! We'll go find a book after this. I promise we'll read for a bit. Yeah, and maybe we can even make up our own stories like the ones we read, but with Lego Ninjago characters. That sounds like a great idea! I'd love to hear the stories you come up with. Now, let's make a deal: thirty more minutes on the tablets, and then we switch to reading. Okay? Okay, deal! Deal! Wonderful. I'll go make some hot chocolate for us to enjoy while we read. It'll be a nice treat after your screen time.

Alright girls, I'm so glad we're all together again. I've missed you both so much since you've been back from your holiday. How was it, really? I want all the details. It was amazing, Mum. The beach was stunning and the food was incredible. We had the best time just relaxing and soaking up the sun. Although, I have to say, the hotel room was a bit of a letdown. Well, I was thinking we could go into town and do some shopping. I need to pick up a few things for the store and it would be nice to have some company. Yeah, that sounds like a good idea. I could do with getting out and about a bit. And maybe we could grab some lunch at that new café that just opened up? That sounds perfect. I've been wanting to try that place out. Why don't we make a day of it and go to the park afterwards? The weather is supposed to be nice, so it would be lovely to get some fresh air. That sounds like a great plan, Mum. I'll just go get my bags and we can head out. And I'll go make some more coffee, so we can take some with us on the go. Brilliant. I'll just tidy up in here

I'm so hungry, I could eat a whole sandwich shop. What's good here, have you guys tried anything? Yeah, I had a decent chicken sandwich from that place over there last week. Not bad, but not amazing either. You know what's been really good lately? The new sandwiches they've been serving at school. Ugh, don't even get me started on the school food. I mean, I know some people like it, but honestly, it's just not my thing. Although, I did hear that Alex from our class joined the army cadets. Have you guys heard anything about that? Yeah, I saw him in his uniform the other day. He seems really into it. I'm not sure I could do it, though. All that discipline and waking up early... no thanks. I know what you mean. I've been thinking about joining the debate team instead. At least that way, I can argue about stuff that actually matters, like racism and social justice. That's really cool! I've been thinking about joining the school council, actually. We could use some more student voices, especially when it comes to stuff like school prefects and how they're chosen. Yeah, that's true. I feel like sometimes the prefects can be really unfair. Like, remember when they gave us detention for being late to class, but then they let their friends off with a warning? Exactly! It's all about who you know, unfortunately. Speaking of which, have you guys seen that new TV show, "The Undoing"? It's so good. Oh, yeah! I binge-watched the whole series over the holidays. I'm obsessed with the characters. We should have a viewing party and play some cards afterwards. Sounds like a plan to me. I've been practicing my poker face, so you guys are in trouble. By the way, has anyone seen the new Marvel movie? Yeah, I saw it last weekend. It was amazing! The special effects were insane. Although, I have to say, the storyline was a bit predictable. I know what you mean. I felt like I'd seen it all before. But hey, at least it was entertaining. So, what's everyone doing for the holidays this year? I'm going to visit my family in Cornwall. We always have a great time down there. How about you guys? I'm actually going to France with my family.

Oh my gosh, I'm so done with school this week. I had the most boring physics lesson with Mr. Johnson. He just drone's on and on, doesn't he? I know, right? I was literally falling asleep in class. And to make matters worse, our form tutor, Mrs. Thompson, gave us a massive lecture about our behaviour during assembly. Like, what's the point of assembly anyway? Exactly! I'm surprised he didn't get expelled on the spot. Anyway, have you seen that film "17 Again"? I watched it over the weekend and it's so funny. I think we should watch it together soon. Yeah, I've seen it! I loved it. Zac Efron is just adorable. But yeah, we should totally have a movie night soon. Maybe we can even get some others to join us. By the way, how's your English reading lessons going? I'm really struggling with the coursework. It's going alright, I suppose. I'm just finding it hard to understand some of the books we're reading. Like, have you read that thing by Shakespeare? It's all so confusing. But our teacher, Mrs. Lee, is really nice and she's always willing to help us out. Ugh, don't even get me started on Shakespeare! I mean, I know it's a classic and all, but it's just so hard to follow. And the language is all weird and stuff. But yeah, Mrs. Lee is really nice. I've had her for a few lessons and she's always making sure we understand the material. Definitely. So, have you talked to Emily lately? I haven't seen her around school much and I'm starting to get a bit worried. We should go visit her after school sometime. Actually, I saw her yesterday and she's doing alright. She's just been really busy with her family stuff and hasn't had much time for school. But yeah, we should definitely go visit her soon. Maybe we can even convince her to come to our movie night. Sounds like a plan to me! And hey, speaking of people at school, have you noticed how weird Mr. Johnson is?

Blud, I'm so done with this semester, I need a break. Have you guys thought about our summer plans yet? I've been thinking about it nonstop! I was considering going to Transylvania, I've heard it's amazing. What do you think, Alex? Ooh, that sounds fascinating! I've always wanted to visit Dracula's castle. But aren't you worried it might be a bit... spooky? Ha! I love spooky stuff. And it's not just about the castle, the whole region is supposed to be stunning. We could make a road trip out of it. Apparently, Tom's been thinking about getting laser eye surgery. Can you imagine? Bugger me! That's a big decision. I've heard it's a game-changer, though. My cousin got it done and she loves it. That's a lot of money to drop on a whim. I know, I know, but think about how convenient it would be. No more contacts, no more glasses... it's tempting, trust me.

Alright kids, gather 'round. We need to finalize the playlist for grandma's party this weekend. What kind of music do you both think she'd like? We'll make sure to capture all the fun moments. Now, let's get started on those sandwiches and make it a lovely day. This is going to be the best day ever!

I'm tellin' ya, I'm so proud of you young'uns gettin' them exam results. I remember when I was at school, we didn't have all these new-fangled exams like you do now. I've just started takin' 'em, and I'm determined to pass me test this time! Oh, that's wonderful, dear! You'll be drivin' like a pro in no time, I'm sure. Though, I have to say, I'm a bit worried about you tweetin' photos of yourself behind the wheel...you're not plannin' on drivin' and tweetin' at the same time, are you? Oh, no, no, no! I'm not that silly, dear! Though, I do like takin' photos of me food...speakin' of which, who's ready for some pizza and chocolate roulade? Ooh, I am! I'm starvin'! Me too!

I'm so glad we're having a relaxing morning with a game of Chinese chess, it's been a while since we've had a chance to catch up like this. How's your day been so far, dear? I'm telling you, it's been a wild ride teaching those students English as a foreign language. I've had my fair share of challenges, but it's so rewarding to see them progress. I've been doing it part-time, you know, just to keep myself busy since I'm not fully employed. I can imagine! I've had my own set of experiences teaching English abroad. The students here in Poland are so eager to learn, it's lovely. But I have to say, the bureaucracy can be a bit of a headache at times. Have you been following the news back home about the student loan crisis? Oh, yes! It's appalling, isn't it? The way the government is handling it is just not right. I mean, I didn't have to deal with student loans when I was in university, but I can only imagine how stressful it must be for the young people these days. And to think that they're still expected to pay back those loans even after they've graduated and are trying to start their careers... it's just not fair. Exactly! And it's not just the students who are suffering. The teachers are feeling the pinch too. I've got friends back home who are struggling to make ends meet, and it's all because of the pension reforms. Blimey, this Passover Seder is shaping up to be a real bash, innit? Your mum's cooking is always top-notch, but this year it's something special. Thanks, Alex! Alright, mates, I'm counting down the days until my holiday in Spain. Two weeks of sun, sea, and sangria. I'm planning to visit Barcelona and take a stroll along La Rambla. Ah'm tellin' ye, pet, Newcastle's goin' doon this season. They can't seem to get their act together, like. I mean, have ye seen their defense? It's like a sieve, so it is. Ah, grandma, I'm so glad we're havin' a brew together today. I've been meanin' to ask you, have you seen any good films lately? Alright, kids, who's excited for Pancake Day tomorrow? We're going to make some delicious pancakes in class and learn about its history. I am! I am! I'm so glad we decided to get Chinese food tonight, I've been craving it all week. What's your favourite dish, Alex? Ah, that's a tough one. I think I'd have to go with the Kung Pao chicken. Alright, everyone, I think it's time for some afternoon tea. I've got a fresh pot of Earl Grey and some lovely biscuits. Ooh, sounds perfect. I'm so glad we're all together today. Ah'm tellin' thee, it's been a mad week at work. We've 'ad a conference every day, an' I'm fair knackered. How's life as a labourer treatin' yer, then, lad? It's been alright, I s'pose. I'm tellin' you, mate, I've had the most interestin' conversation with some Chinese guests I met at the language teachin' workshop last week. It's nice to have a bit of green space in the middle of the city. Although, I have to say, I'm gettin' a bit peckish. Alrigh' then, pet, how's it goin'? I were thinkin' we could head doon to me mam's for dinner the night, she's been askin' after ye. Ah, sounds like a plan, I've not seen your mum in ages. What's she cooking up for us? Hopefully not that infamous beef stew of hers. Oh, ye never know, she might just have a surprise in store for us! But, aye, it'll be canny to catch up wi' her. An' we can tell her about the plans fer the weekend, too. Definitely, I've been meaning to ask her about that garden of hers, I've got a few ideas for my own place and I know she's always been green-thumbed. Don't want to get caught ootside in the rain, do we? An' I've got to make sure everything's sorted at work before I take the day off. Fair point, we don't want a repeat of last time. I'll have a look at the forecast when we get back. Oh, and I almost forgot, I spoke to Tom the other day and he's keen to join us for the hike. Is that alright with you? Course it is, the more the merrier, I say! Tom's a top bloke, it'll be grand to have him along. We should give him a ring later an' confirm the details. An' maybe we can persuade him to bring some of them fancy sandwiches he's always talkin' about. Will do. Now, shall we get moving? We don't want to be late for your mum's dinner. Ah'm tellin' thee, it's been a right tough week. Ah've been co-ordinatin' this big conference at work an' ah've come down wi' a nasty cold. Me throat's been killin' me all day. Sorry to hear that, Emily. You should've taken it easy instead of pushin' yourself too hard. Do you want another cup of tea? I can put the kettle on. Thanks, Alex, that's really kind of you. But ah'm tryin' to cut down on me tea intake, y'know, for me health an' all that. So, how's work been treatin' you? Still enjoyin' the labourin' job? It's alright, I s'pose. Can't complain. Family's important, an' it's great that you're supportin' her through this tough time. We should all get together soon, maybe have a night out or sommat, an' take her mind off things.

I'm telling you, it's been a nightmare at work this week. Our team leader has been breathing down my neck, making sure I meet all the deadlines for the project. I'm not surprised he's moved on so quickly. But poor Sarah, she deserves so much better than him. We should organize a night out with her soon, take her mind off things. Definitely. Alright kids, settle down for a bit. We were talking about good versus evil in legends and folk tales. What do you think about it, Emily? Do you think there's always a clear distinction between the two? I don't know, miss...I mean, mum. Sometimes the bad people can seem nice at first, but then they do something bad. Like in that story about the wolf and the three little pigs. Yeah! And sometimes the good people can do something bad by accident. Like when I broke my toy and then I felt bad about it. That's a great point, Jack. It's not always easy to know what's good and what's bad. And sometimes people can make mistakes without meaning to. But in stories, it's often more clear-cut. The good guys are usually the heroes, and the bad guys are the villains. But what about the stories where the bad guys have a reason for being bad? Like, maybe they were treated unfairly or something. Does that make them less bad? Ah, that's a great question, Emily. It's true that sometimes people do bad things because they feel like they have no other choice, or because they've been treated badly themselves. That doesn't necessarily make their actions right, but it can make them more understandable. And it's always important to try to understand why people do the things they do. I don't get it. If someone is being mean to me, I don't think it's okay for me to be mean back to them. That would make me a bad guy too! That's a very mature way of thinking, Jack. You're right, just because someone is being mean to us, it doesn't give us an excuse to be mean back. We should always try to be kind and fair, even if others aren't. But what about in stories, mum? Can the bad guys ever become good guys? Well, in some stories, yes. It's possible for characters to change and learn from their mistakes. Maybe they realize that what they're doing is hurting people, and they want to make amends. Or maybe they meet someone who helps them to see things from a different perspective. Like when I said sorry to Sarah for taking her toy without asking! Exactly, Jack!

Alright, how was everyone's day? I had a bit of a long one at the office, trying to get those reports done for the meeting tomorrow. It was good, thanks. I'm telling you, John, I've been having the most dreadful knee problems lately. I'm telling you, it's been a wild semester. I've had some of the most talented students I've ever had the pleasure of teaching, but also some of the most challenging.
